primary_diagnosis_treated: Advanced diabetic kidney disease (CKD‑5) with type 2 diabetes

medications.purpose: Glucose lowering in CKD eGFR 20‑30 mL/min/1.73 m²; low hypoglycaemia risk
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends a DPP‑4 inhibitor for CKD eGFR 20‑30 when metformin unsuitable (by‑comorbidity section). Linagliptin requires no renal dose adjustment.

medications.dose: 5 U at bedtime; titrate by 2 U every 3 days to fasting glucose 4‑7 mmol/L
medications.purpose: Provide basal insulin after reduction of pre‑mixed insulin to avoid hypoglycaemia (HbA1c 3.1 %).
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 insulin regimen: basal insulin is first‑choice when insulin is required (insulin_regimens).

medications.purpose: Hypertension control and renoprotection in CKD with proteinuria.
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive in CKD (by‑comorbidity hypertension).

medications.purpose: Adjunct antihypertensive to achieve BP <140/80 mmHg.
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 advises combination therapy when ACE‑I alone does not achieve target BP.

medications.purpose: Contraception; no interaction with diabetes agents.
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 does not contraindicate hormonal contraception in diabetes; continue as prescribed.
CKD management guidelines (aligned with NICE) recommend ESA for anaemia when Hb <10 g/dL.

medications.duration: Ongoing, review lipid panel in 12 weeks
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction; likely QRISK ≥10 % given age, CKD, metabolic syndrome.
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28: offer statin if QRISK ≥10 % (monitoring section).

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive glucose‑lowering effect may increase risk of hypoglycaemia.
interactions_checked.action: Reduce basal insulin dose as outlined; monitor self‑blood glucose closely for 2 weeks.

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential additive blood‑pressure lowering effect; monitor BP and renal function.
interactions_checked.action: Check BP at each visit; adjust dose if symptomatic hypotension.

contraindications.drug: Metformin hydrochloride 500 mg extended‑release oral tablet
contraindications.reason: eGFR likely <30 mL/min/1.73 m² (CKD stage 4‑5); risk of lactic acidosis per NICE NG28.

assumptions_warnings: Exact eGFR not provided; assumed 15‑30 mL/min/1.73 m² based on creatinine 2.8 mg/dL and CKD stage 4‑5.
QRISK score not available; assumed ≥10 % given age, CKD, metabolic syndrome – statin recommended pending formal calculation.
Liver function tests (ALT/AST, bilirubin) not reported; obtain before initiating atorvastatin.
Serum potassium not reported; check before continuing or up‑titrating lisinopril.
Allergy history not provided; verify no hypersensitivity to linagliptin or statin.
BMI and weight not provided; consider GLP‑1 RA if obesity becomes a target later.
treatment_summary: Stop metformin (contraindicated in advanced CKD). Reduce pre‑mixed insulin and initiate low‑dose basal insulin (glargine) with close glucose monitoring. Start linagliptin 5 mg daily as renal‑safe glucose‑lowering therapy. Continue ACE‑I and amlodipine for BP and renal protection, and maintain contraception and ESA therapy. Initiate atorvastatin 40 mg for cardiovascular risk pending QRISK calculation. Provide diabetes education, diet, exercise, and regular monitoring of HbA1c, renal function, electrolytes, lipids, BP, and foot/retinal health.
